subsystems.name: Compute core array
subsystems.role: hundreds of thousands of identical small processors laid out in a grid, plus a fabric that lets any core reach any other.

subsystems.name: Defect tolerance layer
subsystems.role: routes around manufacturing flaws so a whole wafer still works.
parts: routing tables that isolate bad cores
clock and power gating of dead regions

subsystems.name: Reticle-stitched interconnect
subsystems.role: joins regions printed in separate lithography exposures into one continuous fabric.

subsystems.name: Power delivery
subsystems.role: feeds a very large die at low voltage and very high current without voltage droop.
parts: thousands of power and ground connections

subsystems.name: Cooling assembly
subsystems.role: removes heat from an entire wafer that expands when hot.
parts: bonded cold plate with matched thermal expansion

subsystems.name: Package and system interface
subsystems.role: connects the wafer to memory, host and network.

buildSteps.title: Design for repetition
buildSteps.detail: The chip is drawn as a repeated tile of identical cores so errors can be mapped and bypassed; spares are built in from the start.

buildSteps.title: Print across reticle fields
buildSteps.detail: A wafer is far larger than one lithography field, so the stepper exposes overlapping fields and dedicated stitch structures join the wiring where fields meet.

buildSteps.title: Fabricate the full wafer
buildSteps.detail: Standard leading-node CMOS processing runs on a 300 mm wafer — and the wafer is kept whole instead of being diced.

buildSteps.title: Test every core
buildSteps.detail: Probe stations map good and bad cores across the whole wafer, producing a defect map.

buildSteps.title: Program the routing
buildSteps.detail: The defect map is burnt into on-wafer tables so the interconnect detours around faulty regions and the wafer behaves as one device.

buildSteps.title: Bond the cold plate
buildSteps.detail: A cooling plate engineered to expand at the same rate as silicon is bonded across the full wafer so thermal stress does not crack it.

buildSteps.title: Assemble and power
buildSteps.detail: The wafer is mounted in a package, wired to a board carrying many-phase power converters and connected to memory and the host system.

buildSteps.title: Validate as a system
buildSteps.detail: The whole unit is tested under sustained load for performance, power and reliability — behaviour that single-die testing cannot predict.

prerequisites.why: dense interconnect between cores is what makes wafer-scale bandwidth possible.
no single exposure field can cover a wafer; fields must be joined reliably.

prerequisites.tech: Redundancy and defect mapping at wafer level
prerequisites.why: every wafer has flaws, so yield must come from routing around them rather than discarding the wafer.
a hot silicon wafer several hundred millimetres wide expands enough to crack if bonded to ordinary metal.
a whole wafer draws hundreds of amps at under a volt, which demands tight power integrity.
probing and handling an undiced wafer is unusual and the tooling is specialised.

pathway.milestone: single-wafer engines in commercial AI systems with tens of gigabytes of on-chip memory

pathway.unlocks: larger models and less time waiting on external memory.
